name: Gaillardia

project_scope.note: All four are canonical in current manifest. Preserve G. aestivalis provisional range/HOLD and the earlier B075 notes; canonical admission is separate from native-range certification.

study_strategy.warning: Color and ray number vary. G. aestivalis is canonical but its target-zone range status remains provisional/HOLD; preserve the earlier scientific decision. Flower-only photos cannot prove leaf placement or mature fruit traits.
teaching_order: Head front: rays and disk florets

curation_status.genus_lesson: four canonical species reconciled; photo-led comparison provisional

b075_study_strategy.warning: Ray color alone is unreliable in Gaillardia. Habit and stem/leaf architecture are especially useful.

quick_split: G. suavis — perennial basal rosette, long nearly leafless peduncles, fragrant heads, rays reduced or absent; local PASS.
G. amblyodon — annual leafy plant with mostly maroon/red rays lacking bright yellow tips; local PASS.
G. aestivalis — leafy hairy stems, variable yellow/orange/partial rays, upper leaves may clasp; range HOLD.
G. pulchella — existing firewheel anchor, annual with strongly bicolored red/yellow rays.

look_here_first: FIRST inspect where the leaves grow: leafy branching flowering stems versus a basal rosette with long nearly naked stalks. SECOND look at the flower head from front and side: count ray florets (including absent/reduced rays), inspect disk florets and the layered phyllaries beneath the head. THIRD check mature cypsela/pappus when ambiguous. Do not key by yellow or maroon alone.

comparison_cards.title: Fragrant gaillardia versus leafy blanketflowers
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Follow the entire flowering stalk down to the plant base.
comparison_cards.difference: G. suavis has a perennial basal rosette and long largely leafless peduncles, often with reduced or absent rays. The other three usually bear leaves on branching flowering stems.
comparison_cards.caution: Rays may be reduced in other species too; verify whole plant and basal leaves.

comparison_cards.title: Maroon blanketflower versus firewheel
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare intact heads and leaves on several plants, not one ray.
comparison_cards.difference: G. amblyodon commonly has mostly maroon rays; G. pulchella often has red rays with conspicuous yellow tips. Both are leafy and can overlap in appearance.
comparison_cards.caution: Ray pigmentation alone is not a secure identification; matched phyllary, stem and mature fruit characters need further keyed verification.

comparison_cards.title: Lanceleaf blanketflower versus firewheel
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Compare mature stem leaves, their attachment and full plant architecture.
comparison_cards.difference: G. aestivalis is generally a short-lived perennial with hairy leafy stems and sometimes clasping upper leaves; G. pulchella is commonly annual with variable lobed lower leaves.
comparison_cards.caution: Both can show yellow-tipped rays; perenniality and upper-leaf clasping vary. Request regional key confirmation before making a single-trait decision.
